# Claude Code adapter

Generated from the tool-neutral contracts in `spec/agents/`. Regenerate with:

```bash
product agents build
```

To use these in a project, copy them into that project:

```bash
cp -r adapters/claude-code/agents   .claude/agents
cp -r adapters/claude-code/commands .claude/commands
```

## Agents

| Agent | Creates | CLI-enforced | On the model |
|---|---|---|---|
| `product-discovery` | NEED, ASSUM, QUES, RISK | 5 | 5 |
| `product-manager` | OBJ, GOAL, KPI, FEAT, US | 5 | 4 |
| `system-analyst` | TASK, DEC, RISK | 4 | 3 |
| `product-critic` | _nothing_ | 3 | 4 |

## Commands

- `/product:new` — Start a new product workspace and frame the problem
- `/product:discover` — Frame the problem: needs, assumptions, open questions, risks
- `/product:strategy` — Objectives, product goals and measurable KPIs
- `/product:prd` — Compose a PRD from existing nodes, citing their IDs
- `/product:stories` — Features and user stories with testable acceptance criteria
- `/product:plan` — Break accepted stories into technical tasks, decisions and risks
- `/product:review` — Adversarial review: weak reasoning, laundered assumptions, traceability gaps
- `/product:why` — Why does this artifact exist? Show the chain up to a business objective
- `/product:status` — Structural completeness and what rests on unvalidated reasoning
- `/product:check` — Validate the reasoning graph
- `/product:context` — Full reasoning bundle for an artifact, for briefing implementation

The last four are thin wrappers over the deterministic CLI. They call no model to
produce their answer, which is why they can be trusted when the rest cannot.
